findings.title: Use the booking organizer's credentials to update the calendar
findings.body: The authorization check permits attendees and team admins to add guests, but EventManager is constructed with the caller's credentials. For a logged-in attendee with no connected calendar, those credentials cannot update the organizer's existing calendar references. The new guests are saved to the booking, but the organizer's Google/Outlook event remains unchanged. Construct the manager with the booking organizer and their credentials instead.

findings.title: Authorize either team admins or team owners
findings.body: The team authorization check combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&. A team admin who is not the owner therefore fails this check and receives FORBIDDEN when adding guests to another member's booking, unless they are also an attendee. Use || so either privileged team role grants access.

findings.title: Deduplicate guest addresses on the server
findings.body: uniqueGuests only filters addresses already present in the booking; it does not remove duplicates within the submitted array. The server schema also accepts duplicates, so a request containing the same new address twice passes both values to createMany, creating duplicate attendees and sending duplicate invitation emails. The dialog's client-side Set validation does not protect the mutation from direct requests. Enforce uniqueness server-side before inserting guests.

findings.title: Normalize guest addresses before checking the blacklist
findings.body: Blacklist entries are lowercased, but submitted guest addresses are compared without normalization. z.string().email() accepts uppercase characters, so a blacklisted address such as blocked@example.com can be invited by submitting BLOCKED@example.com. Normalize submitted addresses before checking BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS so casing cannot bypass the configured exclusion.

findings.title: Honor disabled standard-email settings for guest additions
findings.body: sendAddGuestsEmails sends host and attendee emails unconditionally and has no event-type metadata parameter. Unlike the scheduled and location-change email helpers, it never checks disableStandardEmails.all.host or disableStandardEmails.all.attendee. Adding a guest consequently sends notifications to recipients whose standard emails were explicitly disabled, including existing attendees, and can duplicate replacement workflow emails. Pass the event-type metadata from the handler and apply the existing email-disable checks.

findings.title: Validate booking status before sending confirmed invitations
findings.body: After finding the booking, the handler checks authorization but never checks its status. An organizer or attendee can therefore add guests to a CANCELLED, REJECTED, or PENDING booking. The subsequent guest-update emails attach an ICS with status CONFIRMED and method REQUEST, sending confirmed invitations for an event whose stored status remains cancelled, rejected, or pending. Reject unsupported booking states before creating attendees or use a status-appropriate notification flow.
